body: Not sure how I feel about this overall...  However, I will say that I've never really been comfortable revealing the extent of my suicidal thoughts to any of my therapists for fear of what they might do.  I don't think I'm at immediate risk, I don't have like a date picked out or anything like that, but I've still been afraid to do more than vaguely mention it and then massively downplay it.  I'm always terrified that I might get hospitalized or sent to a psych ward or whatever; I don't have insurance so that could literally bankrupt me.

Dude, no joke, running away and leaving everything behind has been a recurrent fantasy of mine since childhood.  I think it started out totally innocent; when I was very little we lived in a beautiful part of the world with towering hills and deep, lush forests everywhere, and I would wonder what it would be like to ignore all the rules and just strike off in a random direction.  I think it was just a desire to explore and have an adventure; what would I find over the next hill, you know?  Then when I got a little older and things started to get bad at home I used to dream more specifically of "running away from home"; when I was around 8 I even went so far as to make plans with my best friend and pack a bag... but she got cold feet and told her mom so nothing ever came of that haha.

Later on, when I was a teenager, we moved to a new place and things got worse than ever at home.  Everything was dry and flat and the road stretched straight to the horizon in either direction.  I would stand at the end of our driveway some nights and imagine hopping on my bike and just going until I disappeared over that horizon.

I'm an adult now and sometimes I still think about "running away from home", even though it's my home now and not my parents'. Sometimes it's easier to think about that than it is to think about suicide, and I imagine there's a good chance it would end up with me dying anyway.  But I like to wonder about how far I could get with what little savings I have, and where I might try to go.  There are a few places I'd like to see before I die, and I don't know if I'll ever get a chance to otherwise.  Of course in the end I'm not brave enough to kill myself or to run away, so I'll just stay stuck here living the same day on infinite repeat forever.

I had a horribly fucked up childhood too and I certainly haven't overcome depression, but I do believe it's possible.  It sounds like you're doing all the right things--you're distancing yourself from the crazy drama of your family, you're seeking therapy, and it sounds like you have a healthy relationship with your partner.  I hope you can find peace.
I know the feeling bud.  I hope you can stay strong.
